entries.expected_signal: overflow values are rejected (return FALSE), valid values accepted (return TRUE)

contracts.detail: BEFORE: identical overflow Content-Length values returned TRUE (incorrectly matched as equal, both saturate to G_MAXUINT64). AFTER: returns FALSE (properly rejected via errno==ERANGE). The breach is the intended input contract tightening per RFC 9110.

behavior_differences.before: overflow Content-Length values accepted (saturate to G_MAXUINT64, erroneously match as equal)
behavior_differences.after: overflow Content-Length values rejected (errno==ERANGE, return FALSE)
behavior_differences.evidence: Test output: BEFORE key test returned TRUE, AFTER key test returned FALSE. gcov confirms lines 300-307 are executed.

notes: The patch fixes a bug where g_ascii_strtoull overflow was not detected, allowing invalid Content-Length values to pass validation.
This is an INPUT_CONTRACT_CHANGE: previously accepted overflowed values are now rejected.
All changed lines (5 executable lines) are covered with 11-13 hits.
The existing header-parsing-test suite (12 subtests) passes on both before and after builds.
Behavior difference is confirmed and is the intended effect of the patch (bug fix).

conclusion.rationale: The patch adds errno==ERANGE overflow detection to Content-Length header validation. Previously, overflowed values were silently accepted (both saturating to G_MAXUINT64). Now they are properly rejected. This is an INPUT_CONTRACT_CHANGE: the set of accepted inputs is narrowed. While this is a bug fix per RFC 9110, it changes externally observable behavior - requests with overflowing Content-Length values that were previously accepted will now be rejected. Patch impact coverage: 100% (5/5 executable lines covered).
recommended_actions: Document that overflowing Content-Length values are now rejected per RFC 9110
Verify no downstream consumers depend on overflowed Content-Length values being silently accepted
Include this fix in release notes as a security/correctness improvement
